newsitem.title: GERMANY: Mannesmann confirms talks with Italy's OSR.
newsitem.headline: Mannesmann confirms talks with Italy's OSR.

text.p: Mannesmann AG, the German engineering and telecommunications group, on Friday confirmed it was in talks about taking a stake in Omnitel Sistemi Radiocellulari of Italy.
A Mannesmann spokesman said talks have been underway for several days and the aim was to increase its holding in Omnitel Pronto Italia, the Italian cellular phone operator.
"Talks are underway and they could be concluded today," the spokesman said.
He would not elaborate on the size of the acquisition being discussed or other financial details.
Mannesmann confirms talks with Italy's OSR
The shares in OSR would come from Olivetti, a package of around eight percent that Olivetti acquired from investment bank Lehman Bros, the Mannesmann spokesman later added.
"It centres around the OSR shares that Lehman Bros had held. By taking this stake we will indirectly raise our holding in Omnitel Pronto Italia," he said.
Omnitel Pronto Italia (OPI) Spa is Italy's second GSM cellular phone service manager. Its shareholders are:
-- 70 pct Omnitel Sistemi Radiocellulari Italiani (Olivetti is majority shareholder, then Bell Atlantic, U.S. telecom company CCI Inc, Sweden's Telia).
-- 30 pct Pronto Italia (includes Air Touch, Mannesmann and others)
After considering the stakes in OSR and Pronto Italia, the final shareholdings in Omnitel Pronto Italia are as follows:
Olivetti 41.3 pct
Bell Atlantic 11.3 pct
CCI (Cellular Communication Intl) 10.3 pct
Telia 6.8 pct
Airtouch (via Ati Netherlands Ltd) 15.4 pct
Mannesmann Eurokom 5.9 pct
Others 8.6 pct

Olivetti chief executive officer Roberto Colaninno said last month the company intended to sell an eight percent stake in Omnitel Sistemi Radiocellulari to Germany's Mannesmann but this would not affect Olivetti's control over the company.
Stock market estimates suggest Olivetti could raise some 400 billion lire from the sale of the eight percent Omnitel stake. Olivetti would still retain more than 50 percent of Sistemi Radiocellulari.
-- William Boston, Bonn Newsroom, 49 228 26097150
